scope: Bounded source and native compiler-context probes for AllocateSoundBuffer and SubmitAudio. Complete target function extents compared; no full-DLL equality claimed.
findings: Combining DirectSound/configuration/log definitions in original address order, then adding real preceding HLE/legacy and SIMD/memory definitions, does not change either target body under native C or C++.

Direct PendingBytes references in both preparation calls give the original ESI byte-count / EDI pending-count allocation. The compiler preserves the pending value across the visible ReadAudioMemory implementation; the previous explicit local snapshot was unnecessary.

A separate signed float sample-distance value gives the original 0x2c SubmitAudio frame and observed floating-point operation tree. The routine still has register/scheduling differences and remains unmatched.
Separate inline reset/time helpers, initialization-order variants, ordinary clearing loops, and scalar memset variants do not recover AllocateSoundBuffer.
Default VC7 processor choice is /GB. Explicit /G6 does not change these bodies; /G3, /G4, /Op, /Ow and /Oa do not solve them.
No new volatile qualifier, barrier, padding or artificial retained work was adopted.
The complete, correctly ordered first audio band followed by DirectSound in native C++ also preserves both target mismatches.
/Zi and /Z7 preserve the target bodies when their actual aligned extents are compared; auxiliary COFF code-size records alone exclude natural padding.
An attempted /Gy- control was rejected by this compiler as an unknown /G- option and is not treated as a valid compilation hypothesis.

upstream_audit.finding: Ordinary DirectSound cursor/lock code exists, but no matching buffer-allocation reset or sample conversion pass was found.

probes.extent_note: Debug auxiliary symbols record code size before padding. These diagnostics read the entire naturally aligned section extent, without adding bytes, to compare the same full routine extent as the original.

base_source_note: The frozen control source predates promotion of the sample pass and SubmitAudio refinements. Its target differences are 50 and 440; current adopted source is compared separately in audio-dsound-comparison.json.

native_group6_followup.status: Original-order DS/config C consolidation preserves all57 prior complete bodies. Three unmatched routines remain.
findings: Explicit memset/memcpy intrinsic selection under /Oi-, (void)memset, ZeroMemory and ordinary inline clear helpers do not change either allocation or submission mismatches. Helpers also emit additional unmatched code and are not retained.
Signed long, signed int or unsigned int cursor locals leave SubmitAudio unchanged. An integer sample-distance local worsens differences from421 to427; not retained.
Assigning the default error message before sprintf, in the destination argument, or with both output locals assigned before sprintf grows AudioError from640 to656 bytes; not retained.
No speculative source qualifiers, pragma settings, extra helper functions or artificial work were promoted.
